chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a man who does not wake up at the end of the night until those ten and fifteen have passed: is it more beloved to you that he perform it at the beginning of the night, or that he make it up? He said: No, rather making it up is more beloved to me. I dislike that this be adopted as a habit. And Zurārah used to say: How can he make up a prayer whose time has not yet entered? Its time is only after the middle of the night. As for that which indicates the permissibility of that for the traveler...

key_terms.آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ: the latter part of the night, the preferred time under discussion
key_terms.أَوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ: the beginning of the night, mentioned as an alternative time
key_terms.بَعْدَ نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ: after midnight, identified as the proper time
key_terms.صَلَاةً: the prayer being discussed, namely the night supererogatory prayer
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ: to make up the prayer after missing its proper time

ai.seo_question: Is it better to pray the night nawafil early or make them up later if one fears missing them?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on the nawafil of the night for one who fears not waking in the latter part of the night. The Imam عليه السلام states that making it up is more beloved than habitually performing it at the beginning of the night, while the end notes an indication of permissibility for the traveler.
